prompts.tree-01-oak:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: replacement tree sprite proposal for Shovey Classic, a calm 1990s top-down tile puzzle.
Style: clean professional low-resolution PIXEL ART on a virtual 32 by 32 pixel grid, enlarged with exact nearest-neighbor square pixels. One-pixel dark cool-green outline, limited 6-8 color palette, large coherent shaded clusters, highlights upper left. Cool jade and blue-green foliage, warm brown trunk. Perspective slightly elevated top-down RPG, no isometric tile.
Composition: exactly ONE complete tree centered, about 28 virtual pixels wide and 29 high, visible short trunk with a small root flare at the bottom. Large readable silhouette at 32x32. Genuine transparent background. No grass patch, dirt, floor, scene, border, labels, lettering, swatch panels, watermarks, or extra trees. Clean attractive forms; avoid stippling, visual noise, tiny leaves, muddy colors, photorealism, smooth vector curves, 3D rendering, blur or antialiasing.
Proposal 1 — OAK: one compact rounded oak with a single cohesive gently scalloped canopy, broad upper-left leaf mass, small lower-right shaded leaf lobe, sturdy visible forked trunk. Lush and friendly, exceptionally simple.

prompts.fish-swim-sheet:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: a pixel-art fish swimming sprite sheet for Shovey Classic's blue water tiles.
Create exactly THREE ROWS and FOUR COLUMNS, twelve equally-sized cells, no gaps, no dividers. Each cell is a virtual 32 by 32 pixel canvas; total virtual sheet 128 by 96 pixels, enlarged by nearest neighbor with chunky square pixels. Transparent background everywhere.
Each row is ONE consistent fish design with FOUR consecutive subtle swimming frames, tail moving left/center/right/center. All face RIGHT, head at right, tail at left, body centers perfectly aligned in all four cells.
Row 1: simple bright orange goldfish, pale cream highlight and chunky fan tail.
Row 2: cream koi with two large warm orange patches and a clear forked tail.
Row 3: pale silver-blue minnow with teal back and cream belly, broad readable forked tail.
Top-down view, see fish backs and paired side fins. Each fish body and tail fills about 22 virtual pixels horizontally, about 12 vertically, centered in its cell, dark navy one-pixel outline and tiny eye; 5-7 colors per fish. Fish should look alive, clean and friendly, visually readable over medium blue water, no muddy dark silhouette. Pixel shapes consistent across frames.
Constraints: no water, ripples, environment, tile backgrounds, lettering, labels, borders, grid lines, shadows, extra fish, bubbles or props. No blur, antialiasing, photorealism, 3D or detailed scales. Exactly 12 fish total; 4 poses each for 3 species.
